answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond in a scarce token, then slash that bond when an inlet of reciprocal trades reveals a closed cluster that only exchanges with itself and never earns from established users. A velvet-smooth profile or repeated echo of legitimate activity does not bypass the rule: the cluster must risk real capital for every identity, keep it locked during review, and lose it if flagged. Sybils therefore cost the attacker both funds and time, while honest newcomers can recover their bond by building useful trade history.
